cases.reason: Format identical (SAME AS data-name-1); SR1-SR9 correspond, 2023 SR10 (CONSTANT RECORD) is 2023-only. The rule's subject is a level 77 entry, which 2002 13.1.1 admits only in working-storage, local-storage and linkage (the COMMUNICATION SECTION format takes only communication-description entries, constant entries and record-description entries), so no CD reach for the subject; data-name-1 is confined by SR7 (identical in both) to the file, working-storage, local-storage and linkage sections, so no CD reach for the operand either. 'Elementary item' is the same notion (2002 8.5.1.2). No band, no enumeration, no deferral. Probes at both editions agree: 77 SAME AS a local-storage group and 77 SAME AS a file-section record are refused (COBOL1555), 77 SAME AS a file-section elementary item is accepted.

cases.reason: Format identical (BASED). BASED is confined to level 1/77 entries of linkage, working-storage and local-storage in both editions (2002 13.14.2 SR15, 2023 13.16.3 SR16), so no CD, report or screen reach. Class object has the single category object-reference in both class/category tables (2002 line 'Object | Object-reference', same in 2023); 2023 adds message-tag as a separate class, not object. 2023 SR2 (dynamic-length/variable-length) is 2023-only. Probes at both editions agree: USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE BASED refused in local-storage at level 77 and via TYPE of an object-reference typedef (COBOL1797); a PIC X BASED entry runs (XYZ).

cases.reason: Format identical apart from 2023 rounded-phrase for ROUNDED (a widening). The rule is a keyword synonymy independent of the operand. The reader's scope ('report section only') misses that 2002 SR4 lets identifier-1 name an item of ANY data-division section, which in 2002 includes the communication section; I probed that leg at --std 2002: SOURCES ARE / SOURCE IS a CD-record item print 'MN OP', so the synonymy holds there too. Multi-operand (SOURCE IS a b c vs SOURCES ARE c b a) and ROUNDED forms also agree at both editions ('ABCDEF EF CD AB 1.3 1.3').
